attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts this in his own commentary.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the present-state assertion. The acknowledged scientific and analytics exceptions remain relevant to its scope.

contract.note: Practical usefulness beyond AI is an ordinary reading. Requiring representative deployments fairly respects the acknowledged exceptions. May is an evaluator-selected reference period.

evidence.note: Documents scientific GPU computation, but not representative May 2026 workloads or economics at AI-oriented facilities. Such scientific uses are expressly acknowledged.
This later provider disclosure describes non-AI applications and hardware tradeoffs. It supplies no target-period workload shares or representative economics.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes some practical non-AI applications but does not measure their breadth or economic significance across relevant facilities. Neither narrow usefulness nor substantial alternative usefulness is established.

attribution.note: The statement is Zitron's own qualified assessment.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both the appearance qualifier and the tentative inference about business-model viability.

contract.note: The contract converts a qualified assessment into a categorical no-reduction premise. The plain-reading provision does not permit scoring hedged language.

evidence.note: Measured performance with modeled ownership costs provides contrary evidence to the cost premise. Configuration and precision differences limit generalization; it does not establish industry profitability.

reviews.rationale: The statement explicitly qualifies both its cost assessment and its business-model inference. Policy excludes such hedged claims from scoring, even when relevant contrary evidence exists.

semantics.note: The definite Rubin forecast is preserved, alongside a separate historical Blackwell assertion. The forecast label must not erase that historical component.

contract.note: Comparable-workload cost is an ordinary reading of cheaper. The contract appropriately separates historical benchmark evidence from the documented Rubin deployment needed for early resolution.

evidence.note: NVIDIA reports benchmark-based ownership-cost reductions for Blackwell at matched interactivity. This contradicts the historical component under the contract, but remains a company disclosure of modeled costs.
The provider reports a Rubin deployment, higher throughput and lower session costs. Missing cost calculations and quality controls prevent it from meeting the early-resolution rule.
NVIDIA reports benchmark efficiency and token-cost improvements. This does not document comparable delivered-workload costs in a customer deployment.

reviews.rationale: The Blackwell historical component is contradicted by the reported benchmark cost comparison. The Rubin forecast has no deadline, and neither Rubin disclosure meets the contract's early-resolution requirements. The forecast remains unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron asserts subsidy dependence and unaffordability in his own voice.

semantics.note: The core claim attributes demand to subsidies and retains full-cost pricing as the affordability condition. The possibility language concerns a future business arrangement, not the asserted subsidy dependence.

contract.note: Subsidy-dependent demand and majority affordability are ordinary readings. Cost allocation, user population and the first-quarter reference period are evaluator choices requiring explicit measurement.

evidence.note: Measures compensation required to surrender access, not ability or willingness to pay verified full costs. Consumer value does not settle subsidy dependence.
Available before the cutoff, but its April observations fall outside the selected quarter. Paid subscriptions and price sensitivity do not establish full-cost affordability or subsidy dependence.

reviews.rationale: Neither study connects verified provider costs to representative customer affordability and retention. The packet cannot establish how much demand subsidies cause, whether most users could afford full-cost service, or whether enterprise pressure reflects such prices.
